submitted.rationale: Index 20 (Bi 0.33, Fe 0.17, V 0.50) gave the highest photocurrent of the three measured, 2.71e-5 A. Photocurrent rose steadily as the film moved from Bi-rich to V-rich within the low-Fe, BiVO4-like region: idx17 5.1e-6, idx14 2.39e-5, idx20 2.71e-5. MACE puts hematite on the hull, which argues against Fe-rich films.

rejected.reason: MACE puts hematite on the hull, so Fe-rich films likely separate into Fe2O3, a poor photoanode; not measured

consultations.verdict: MEGNet HSE gaps for the Fe2O3 (2.77 eV) and Bi-oxide (2.34 eV) end members are below the 3.2 eV photon energy, so absorption does not limit anything. This is weak support only; my prior still favours monoclinic BiVO4 (Bi:V ~1:1) with little Fe as the best photoanode phase. Index 14 (Bi .39, V .44, Fe .17) sits near BiVO4 on the slightly V-rich side.

MACE puts hematite on the hull, so Fe-rich films will phase-separate into Fe2O3, which is a poor photoanode. That argues for staying in the low-Fe, Bi~V region. Index 17 (Bi .43, V .41, Fe .16) is closer to BiVO4 stoichiometry than index 14. Mild support.

This PBE gap for a reference oxide tells me nothing about the choice (PBE underestimates gaps, and absorption is not the limit at 3.2 eV). The decision comes from the data: photocurrent rose 5x from idx17 (Bi-rich) to idx14 (V-rich). Index 20 (Bi .33, Fe .17, V .50) continues that trend and has the highest GP mean.
